spot.html_text: The term “stit” is an acronym based on “sees to it that”. The idea is to add, to an ordinary classical propositional language, a new propositional operator ⟦M⟧ , interpreting ⟦M⟧ , where ⟦M⟧ stands for an agent and ⟦M⟧ for a proposition, as ⟦M⟧ sees to it that ⟦M⟧ . (The official notation of the Belnap school is more laborious: [ ⟦M⟧ ].) Note that ⟦M⟧ is allowed to contain nestings of the new operator.

spot.html_text: usually an agent is not able to select one possible future to become the unique actual future, but by his action he can make sure that certain futures, which before his action are possible, are no longer possible after his action.
